values: User opens the Zion Events Place landing page and confirms the main public content loads.

1. Open http://localhost:3000/.
2. Wait for the landing page to load.
3. Review the hero, featured content, event highlights, testimonies, and footer sections.
Landing page returns successfully and uses Zion Events Place branding.
User opens the public navigation menu and sees available public links.

1. Open the home page.
2. Open the main navigation.
3. Confirm Home, Packages, Gallery, About Us, Contact Us, FAQ, Rules, Facilities, Policies, Privacy, Terms, and Testimonies are reachable where shown.
Navigation supports the current public web routes and removes obsolete booking/admin entry points.
User expands the Packages menu and sees each event package option.

1. Open the menu.
2. Hover over or tap Packages.
3. Confirm Weddings, Debuts, Christening, Birthdays, Gender Reveal, and Christmas Party are listed.
All current event package links are present in the navigation.
User navigates to the About Us page.

1. Open /about.
2. Confirm the page title and venue story content display.
Route displays current Zion Events Place content.
User views contact details and social/contact links.

1. Open /contact.
2. Confirm email, phone, social links, and map/location entries are shown.
Contact UI displays usable email, phone, social, and map actions.

1. Open /faq.
2. Confirm FAQ categories and answers display.
3. Expand and collapse a question.
FAQ content is visible and interactive.
User views venue rules and regulations.

1. Open /rules.
2. Confirm rules and regulation content is displayed.
Rules content supports the current venue information flow.
User opens the Privacy Policy page.

1. Open /privacy.
2. Confirm privacy policy content is displayed.
Privacy content is reachable from the public site.
User opens the Terms of Service page.

1. Open /terms.
2. Confirm terms content is displayed.
Terms content is reachable from the public site.
User opens the Weddings package page and reviews package content.

1. Open /events/weddings.
2. Confirm hero, content blocks, package details, flipbook cover, and gallery render.
Wedding package route displays current public package content.
User opens the Debuts package page.

1. Open /events/debuts.
2. Confirm package content, flipbook cover, and gallery render.
Debut package route displays current public package content.
User opens the Christening package page.

1. Open /events/christening.
2. Confirm package content, flipbook cover, and gallery render.
Christening package route displays current public package content.
User opens the Birthdays package page.

1. Open /events/birthdays.
2. Confirm package content, flipbook cover, and gallery render.
Birthday package route displays current public package content.
User opens the Gender Reveal package page.

1. Open /events/gender-reveal.
2. Confirm package content, flipbook cover, and gallery render.
Gender Reveal package route displays current public package content.
User opens the Christmas Party package page.

1. Open /events/christmas-party.
2. Confirm package content, flipbook cover, and gallery render.
Christmas Party package route displays current public package content.
User opens the Facilities page and reviews venue spaces.

1. Open /facilities.
2. Confirm facility sections, images, and venue details display.
3. Check that media loads without broken placeholders.
Facilities route replaces the obsolete booking page scenario.
User opens the Gallery page and browses event media.

1. Open /gallery.
2. Review image and video gallery items.
3. Confirm media cards load and remain usable across categories or sections.
Gallery validates public images and videos after duplicate media cleanup.
User opens the Testimonies page and reviews client feedback.

1. Open /testimonies.
2. Confirm testimony cards display.
3. Confirm featured feedback appears without missing names or content.
Testimony content replaces obsolete calendar availability checks.
User opens the Policies page and reviews venue policy content.

1. Open /policies.
2. Confirm public policy content loads.
3. Confirm page links and section labels are readable.
Policies route is part of the current public information set.
User changes the site theme and sees the public layout update.

1. Open any public page.
2. Toggle between light and dark theme.
3. Confirm text, buttons, cards, and page background remain readable.
Theme behavior remains usable across the client-facing layout.
User views the public navigation on mobile width.

1. Resize the browser to a mobile viewport.
2. Open the navigation menu.
3. Confirm menu links are readable and do not overlap.
Responsive navigation replaces obsolete booking wizard step coverage.
User views package content on tablet and mobile widths.

1. Open any event package page.
2. Resize to tablet and mobile widths.
3. Confirm package cards, gallery media, and flipbook cover remain aligned.
Package browsing remains readable across common screen sizes.
User submits the contact inquiry form with missing required values.

1. Open /contact.
2. Submit the inquiry form with required fields blank.
3. Confirm validation prevents submission and highlights required fields.
Validation checks replace obsolete booking add-on flow coverage.
User submits a complete public inquiry.

1. Open /contact.
2. Enter a valid name, email, phone, event interest, and message.
3. Submit the form and confirm the success or received state displays.
Inquiry submission aligns with the current public inquiry API.
User starts contact actions from the public contact page.

1. Open /contact.
2. Click the email, phone, and map/location actions.
3. Confirm each action opens the expected external handler or link.
Contact actions replace obsolete booking review coverage.
User reviews the footer on public pages.

1. Open the home page.
2. Scroll to the footer.
3. Confirm the footer displays (c) 2026 Zion Events Place. All rights reserved.
Footer branding and year match the current product requirement.
Search engines and shared links receive current Zion page metadata.

1. Open the home page source or browser dev tools.
2. Inspect title and meta description.
3. Confirm metadata uses Zion Events Place and page-relevant copy.
Metadata no longer uses old ZenTra branding.
Keyboard user navigates through public site controls.

1. Open the home page.
2. Use Tab and Shift+Tab across navigation, links, toggles, and buttons.
3. Confirm focus order is visible and logical.
Accessibility coverage replaces obsolete admin login coverage.
Screen reader users receive meaningful labels for interactive controls.

1. Inspect navigation, theme, menu, gallery, and form controls.
2. Confirm icon-only controls include accessible names.
3. Confirm form inputs have associated labels.
Accessible labels replace obsolete admin dashboard coverage.
User sees a graceful message when a feature is unavailable.

1. Trigger or visit a route/state for an unavailable public feature.
2. Confirm the page explains the unavailable state.
3. Confirm the user can navigate back to public content.
Graceful unavailable handling replaces obsolete admin module coverage.
Client retrieves managed public content for public pages.

1. Request the public content API.
2. Confirm the response returns active content records.
3. Confirm the UI renders fallback content if the response is empty.
Covers managed public content used by the client-facing site.
Client retrieves event categories for package browsing.

1. Request the event categories API.
2. Confirm active categories include current public event types.
3. Confirm the package navigation remains stable if no categories are returned.
Category data supports current package browsing.
Client retrieves public event package data.

1. Request the event packages API.
2. Confirm package records include names, descriptions, media, and category references.
3. Confirm the UI ignores inactive or malformed entries.
Package API supports public package pages without booking/payment flows.

1. Request the FAQ categories API.
2. Confirm categories return with display order.
3. Confirm the FAQ page groups questions by category when data exists.
FAQ categories drive public help content.

1. Request the FAQs API.
2. Confirm questions and answers return.
3. Confirm inactive or empty answers do not break the FAQ page.
FAQ data is handled safely by the public client.
Client retrieves popular FAQ records for highlighted help content.

1. Request the popular FAQs API.
2. Confirm highlighted FAQ records display.
3. Confirm the page remains usable if no popular FAQs exist.
Popular FAQ coverage matches the current client API surface.
API rejects an invalid public inquiry payload.

1. Send an inquiry payload with missing name, invalid email, or empty message.
2. Confirm the API returns a validation error.
3. Confirm the client shows the error without losing entered values.
Validation protects public inquiry submission quality.
API accepts a valid public inquiry payload.

1. Send a valid inquiry payload.
2. Confirm the API returns a success response.
3. Confirm the client displays confirmation to the user.
Inquiry handling supports the current contact workflow.
Client retrieves public settings used across the site.

1. Request the settings API.
2. Confirm contact, social, branding, and display settings return where configured.
3. Confirm default values render when settings are missing.
Settings fallback prevents broken public pages.

1. Request the testimonies API.
2. Confirm public testimony records return.
3. Confirm the Testimonies page handles empty results gracefully.
Testimony API supports public social proof content.
Client retrieves featured testimonies for highlighted display.

1. Request the featured testimonies API.
2. Confirm featured records return.
3. Confirm home or testimony sections fall back when no featured records exist.
Featured testimonies remain optional and non-blocking.
System health endpoint reports service availability.

1. Request the health endpoint.
2. Confirm the response indicates the service is available.
3. Confirm the endpoint does not expose sensitive internal data.
Health endpoint is useful for uptime checks without exposing private details.
User still sees useful page content when managed content is unavailable.

1. Simulate an empty or failed public content response.
2. Open the affected public page.
3. Confirm fallback copy or safe empty states display without runtime errors.
Fallback behavior keeps public pages usable during content issues.
User sees a graceful state when package data is unavailable.

1. Simulate failed event package data.
2. Open a package page.
3. Confirm the page shows a helpful unavailable or fallback state.
Package pages avoid blank or broken views when data fails.
User opens public gallery media without broken assets.

1. Open /gallery.
2. Scroll through image and video entries.
3. Confirm media files load from public/images and public/videos.
Public media paths remain valid after duplicate image cleanup.
User sees a flipbook cover for package browsing.

1. Open an event package page.
2. Locate the flipbook or package cover area.
3. Confirm cover media loads and matches the selected package.
Flipbook cover improves current package browsing without booking steps.
User does not encounter missing static images or videos on public pages.

1. Open Home, Gallery, Facilities, and one package page.
2. Inspect page media requests.
3. Confirm there are no 404 responses for referenced public assets.
Static assets remain intact across the client-facing site.
User visits an unknown route and receives a graceful not-found experience.

1. Open an invalid route such as /missing-page.
2. Confirm a not-found page or graceful error state appears.
3. Use navigation to return to the public site.
Unknown routes do not trap the user or expose errors.
Public page fetch errors do not crash the application shell.

1. Simulate an API error for a public content request.
2. Reload the affected page.
3. Confirm the layout remains visible with fallback or retry messaging.
Client-side error handling keeps the site usable.
Shared public links show current Zion page preview details.

1. Inspect Open Graph metadata for Home and one package page.
2. Confirm title, description, and image values exist.
3. Confirm metadata uses Zion Events Place branding.
Social sharing metadata supports the current brand.
User moves between package pages through public links.

1. Open a package page.
2. Use related package or navigation links to switch packages.
3. Confirm route changes and content updates correctly.
Internal links support package discovery without stale routes.
User narrows FAQ content when search or category controls are available.

1. Open /faq.
2. Use available category or search controls.
3. Confirm displayed questions update and empty matches show a clear state.
FAQ controls keep help content scannable.
Public inquiry form resists repeated invalid submissions.

1. Submit invalid inquiry data more than once.
2. Confirm validation remains clear and stable.
3. Confirm no duplicate success messages appear for rejected submissions.
Inquiry form avoids misleading success states for bad input.
Client receives predictable response shapes from public APIs.

1. Request public content, settings, packages, FAQ, and testimonies APIs.
2. Confirm responses contain expected fields.
3. Confirm the client handles missing optional fields safely.
Consistent API shapes reduce runtime issues in public views.
User does not see links to removed booking, payment, chatbot, calendar, or admin workflows.

1. Review public navigation, footer, package pages, and contact page.
2. Search visible links and buttons for removed workflows.
3. Confirm only current public site actions remain.
Tracker scope aligns with the current Zion public web application.

values: Showing initial branding screen at app startup

1. Tap on application icon to launch the app
2. Observe the splash screen
3. Wait for splash screen to complete
User navigates to sign in form

1. From the Let's get started screen
click the sign in button, a sign in form will slide upward from user screen
User navigates to sign up form

1. From the Let's get started screen
click the sign up button,  a sign up form will slide upward from user screen
Users need to register themselves in this mobile application.

1. Go to sign-up form
2. Enter a valid first name (at least 2 characters, no numbers or symbols).
3. Enter a valid last name (same rules apply).
4. Enter a valid email (e.g. user@example.com).
5. Enter a strong password (e.g. min 6 characters, includes 1 uppercase letter and 1 number).
6. Type the confirmation of your new password.                                                             
7. Click the Sign up button.
8. A modal will pop up, just click the "Got it!" button  after reading the message.
9. Check email for email verification
10. Confirm email
Email, First Name, Last Name, Password
Users need to register themselves in this mobile application.

1. Go to sign-up form
2. Click "sign-up using Google account"
3. Select your Google account to sign-up
4. Wait for the sign-up authentication that will pop-up after signing up
Connect the hardware component to the mobile application.

1. Turn on the hardware component.
2. Open the device's bluetooth to pair and connect to the mobile device where the application is installed.
3. Open the mobile application to search and pair to the hardware device's bluetooth.
